title: dynamic-batching-seqlen-bucketing-padding-heuristics-v17
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce wasted work caused by padding across dynamic request distributions and improve end-to-end throughput and tail latency for multi-tenant workloads. This PR implements a sequence-length aware bucketing and padding-minimization heuristic for the continuous dynamic batching pipeline in the serving runtime. Approach: 1) Introduce a lightweight bucketer that groups incoming requests into buckets by quantized sequence-length ranges (configurable bins), 2) Within a batch slot, schedule buckets to minimize aggregate padding while maintaining latency SLOs by using a greedy scheduler with a per-batch padding budget, 3) Extend the kernel selector to prefer kernels tuned for the target max_seq of the formed micro-batch to reduce kernel switching overhead, 4) Improve KV-cache lookup/reuse by tracking bucket affinity so repeated short-prefix requests keep cache locality, 5) Add runtime flags and a feature gate (--seqlen-bucketer=enabled|disabled|aggressive) and per-route overrides to preserve backwards compatibility. Results: internal perf runs on a mixed-production trace (50% short chat, 30% long context, 20% embedding-like) show ~14-18% throughput increase under 95th-percentile latency SLOs and ~7-10% reduction in average tokens-per-request compute due to reduced padding. The implementation is conservative by default to avoid regressions for latency-sensitive tenants. Changes include new telemetry (batch_padding_ratio, bucket_skew, seqlen_bucket_size) and a small operator-visible config surface. Checklist: - [x] design doc (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2173/dynamic-batching-by-sequence-length) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] perf benchmarks and comparison script - [x] feature gate and per-route opt-out - [x] docs updated (ops + tuning) Rollout plan: gated rollout behind feature flag; enable for canary fleet (10% traffic) for 48h and monitor batch_padding_ratio, p95 latency, and error rate; then ramp to 100% if within thresholds. Backwards compatible: default is disabled for existing clusters; enabling requires runtime config change only. Risks: aggressive bucketing can increase p95 if misconfigured for adversarial input distributions; mitigated by the conservative default and auto-fallback to existing batching. Links: design doc and perf artifacts attached in commits.

review_comments: Diego Morales (review): Nice work. A few high-level concerns: 1) how does this interact with per-tenant latency SLOs? 2) can we avoid additional kernel switches on mixed batches? Please add telemetry and a fallback path.
Aisha Patel (author): Added per-route opt-out and a conservative default mode; kernel selector now prefers kernels by bucket and has a fast-path to reuse existing kernel when padding budget exceeded.
Lena Chen (review): Tests look good but add a synthetic adversarial test where many long requests arrive in short bursts; also please add comments on time complexity of the scheduler.
Aisha Patel (author): Added adversarial integration test and documented scheduler complexity O(n log k) in the header comments.
Marcus Green (review): CI perf check initially flagged a regression at high concurrency. Can we add a micro-batching threshold to avoid thrashing?
Aisha Patel (author): Added a micro-batch threshold and updated scheduler to prefer filling up to a configurable target to reduce thrash; re-ran perf suite and results improved.
release_notes: Added sequence-length aware bucketing to the dynamic batching pipeline. Default disabled; can be enabled via runtime flag --seqlen-bucketer. Improves throughput and reduces padding-related compute for mixed-length request distributions. New telemetry: batch_padding_ratio, bucket_skew, seqlen_bucket_size.
